Before
 Hon'Ble Smt. Justice Anuradha Shukla

On The 15 th Of July, 2024
 Misc. Criminal Case No. 27795 of 2024
 Kisanu Singh Uikey
 Versus
 The State Of Madhya Pradesh
 Appearance:
 Shri Siddharth Seth - Advocate for applicant.
 Shri Dilip Shrivastava - Government Advocate for respondent
 Order

This is first application filed by the applicant under Section 439 of the Code of Criminal Procedure for grant of regular bail relating to FIR/Crime No.785/2022 dated 10.12.2022 registered at Police Station Shahpur, District Betul for an offence punishable under Sections 420, 409, 34 of IPC.
Learned counsel for applicant has submitted that applicant is innocent and has been falsely implicated in the crime in question.
The applicant is in custody since 16.03.2024 and trial will take considerable time to conclude.
He further submits that applicant is permanent resident of district and there is no likelihood of his absconding from the clutches of law or tampering with prosecution evidence.
He also submits that the applicant is ready to furnish adequate surety and shall abide by all the directions and conditions which may be imposed by this Court.
Upon these grounds, the applicant may be released on bail.
Learned counsel for the State has opposed the bail application and prayed for its rejection.
Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the case-diary.

This first bail application has been argued on the ground that applicant was not named in the FIR and he did not have any role to verify whether the beneficiaries were genuine, whether the construction work was satisfactorily in progress, whether the bank account details of beneficiaries were correct or not,
etc.
According to him, after all the administrative sanctions, he was supposed to use his digital signature for making payment, which he did.

State has opposed the application on the ground that all the payments to ineligible persons were Kisanu Singh Uikey vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 15 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/54133237/
1 made on the basis of digital signature of application authorizing the payment.

sentences.text: Case diary has been perused.
The specific role assigned to the applicant posted as Assistant Account Officer has not been mentioned in any circular or government documents.

The statements of CEO Janpad Panchayat Shahpur namely Firdous Shah recorded under Section 161 CrPC are available on record, which suggest that after generation of order sheet the fourth login is used which is of Assistant Account Officer.
According to these statements in this login, only FTO number is displayed along with the amount due to be paid and the name of the beneficiary.
The statements further disclose that other details about mismatch or any information about errors are not displayed in this log in.
Thus, if any error was committed at the time of registration of beneficiary that error was not supposed to be reflected at the time of using fourth login.
Considering these statements and the role assigned to applicant under the scheme, this bail application is allowed.

It is directed that the applicant shall be released on bail upon his furnishing a personal bond in the sum of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty Thousand Only) with one solvent surety in the like amount to the satisfaction 3 MCRC-27795-2024 of the trial Court concerned for his appearance before the said Court on all such dates as may be fixed in this regard during pendency of the trial.
It is further directed that the applicant shall comply with the provisions of Section 437(3) of Cr.P.C.
Accordingly, this M.Cr.C. stands allowed and disposed of.
